title: Coordinate Geometry
tagline: Year 3 — Distance, section formula, slope, equation of a line and area of a triangle from coordinates

introduction.overview: Coordinate geometry places points on a grid so that geometric questions become algebra. This chapter covers the distance formula, midpoint and section formula, slope of a line, equations of lines, parallel and perpendicular conditions, and the area of a triangle from vertex coordinates.
introduction.placementRelevance: Distance, slope and area questions are short formula problems that appear regularly in aptitude and technical rounds.
introduction.realWorldContext: Maps, GPS navigation, computer graphics and CAD all use coordinates.

learningObjectives: Use the distance and midpoint formulas
Find slopes and equations of lines
Use conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines
Find the area of a triangle and test collinearity

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The point (x, y) lies x units along the horizontal axis and y units along the vertical axis. The slope measures steepness.

coreDefinitions: Distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂): √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²].
Line: y = mx + c, or y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Parallel lines: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular lines: m₁ m₂ = −1.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The distance formula is Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical differences. Slope is rise over run.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Subtract coordinates to get the horizontal and vertical differences first; every formula uses them.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Section formula
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: ((m x₂ + n x₁)/(m + n), (m y₂ + n y₁)/(m + n))

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Triangle area
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|

mainNarrative: To find the distance between (1, 2) and (4, 6), take Δx = 3 and Δy = 4, so the distance is √(9 + 16) = 5.
The point dividing (1, 2) and (7, 8) in the ratio 1 : 2 is ((1 × 7 + 2 × 1)/3, (1 × 8 + 2 × 2)/3) = (3, 4). The midpoint is (4, 5).
The slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 6) is 4/3. A line perpendicular to it has slope −3/4. Parallel lines have equal slopes.
The line through (1, 2) with slope 3 is y − 2 = 3(x − 1), that is y = 3x − 1. The intercept form x/a + y/b = 1 gives intercepts a and b directly.
The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3) is ½ |0 + 4(3 − 0) + 0| = 6. Three points are collinear exactly when this expression is 0.

deepDiveAspects.title: Distance from a point to a line
deepDiveAspects.content: The distance from (x₀, y₀) to ax + by + c = 0 is |a x₀ + b y₀ + c|/√(a² + b²).

deepDiveAspects.title: Centroid
deepDiveAspects.content: The centroid of a triangle is the average of the three vertices.

solvedExamples.title: Section formula
solvedExamples.question: Find the point that divides the line joining (1, 2) and (7, 8) in the ratio 1 : 2.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The point is one-third of the way from (1, 2).

solvedExamples.title: Perpendicular line
solvedExamples.question: Find the equation of the line through (2, 3) perpendicular to 2x + y = 5.

solvedExamples.title: Triangle area
solvedExamples.question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (5, 1) and (3, 6).
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The determinant formula gives the same value.

shortcutMethods.title: Difference first

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write Δx and Δy once; distance, slope and section points all follow from them.

rulesForApplication: Use a horizontal base if available.

commonMistakes.mistake: Swapping x and y in slope
Wrong order in the section formula
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: m : n assigned to the wrong end.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: m goes with the second point.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Check that the point satisfies the line equation.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Use the horizontal or vertical side as the base.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Many coordinate problems are triples in disguise.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I find the distance between two points?
Can I write the equation of a line?
